title: Jacoby Brissett has hit Trey McBride for two catches today that were impressive for both the pass and the catch. On the first, Brissett was on the move to his left and slung it side-armed to the sideline, where McBride came down with it. On the second, Brissett pinpointed the throw low and right at the sideline where only a diving McBride could get it. It sure seems like that connection has picked up where it left off.

title: Watching Liverpool-Wrexham play at Yankees Stadium (on what looks like a minifield, but I digress), reminds me of one of the coolest stories my grandfather told me. He played semi-pro soccer in NYC for years and was a goalie -- a pretty good one at that. He had the good fortune of playing in the old, original Yankee Stadium for a game and one of the goals was right at first base. Every time my grandfather would dive for a ball, a groundskeeper who sat right next to the net, would run out and rake the field to makes sure the dirt didn't get all messed up for none other than Lou Gehrig. My grandfather loved that story.

title: “He came back in phenomenal shape with his weight, with his conditioning test. Even with that contract still looming, he worked his ass off, and I'm proud of him for that. It shows you the type of guy he is and he'll continue to be and excited for him to play ball. I’m just really happy for him and his family. He's worked his butt off to get rewarded the way he is. And like Howie said, we're paying you for what you're going to do in the future, and we have that confidence in him. I've really enjoyed getting to know Jalen more and more each year. The time that I've spent with him, he's put his head down, he's worked, he's made impactful plays, and we look for that to continue. He's a heck of a football player that demands a lot of attention by the opposing offense. So, to be able to have him locked up-- we know what that creates for the opposing offense. I know as a former offensive coordinator the problems that a player at that position with that talent creates and the things that you have to do for him game plan-wise. You're just excited that that portion's out of the way and you're able to go and focus completely on football, which he has, which I give him a lot of credit. He's focused so much on football. “ -Nick Sirianni on Jalen Carter’s record contract. Jalen Carter says his shoulders are better and they are where they need to be after playing through the injuries last year. https://t.co/3nX1gLnAK7

title: Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 3: - Coming off a Tuesday jog through, the Niners had their longest and perhaps most daunting practice yet Wednesday. It's by design. They have a new practice regiment they're trying out in this year's camp. They will do two days of practice, a jog through, a "high" (long) practice and then a day off. The plan is to then repeat that cycle as camp goes a long. If the hope was to help reduce injuries, the early returns aren't promising but there's a long way to go still. - Speaking of scheduling, the Niners will be off tomorrow then are expected to be in their first fully padded practice on Friday. Thus, this will be the last caveat about the lack of pads for this training camp as they were not in them again today. - Once again, coach Kyle Shanahan seems to be following the same routine each day. He came out just before 11 o'clock today during team drills and stayed through the end. It's still unclear how close he is to being back to full duty after his car crash but it appears to be trending the right direction. - New injuries to the list: WR Ricky Pearsall (right knee) did not practice and the Niners are concerned about it. They're "exploring all options" which presumably includes surgical options. A tough early blow for Pearsall, who is entering an important third season. S Malik Mustapha has a hamstring strain, which is also unfortunate given he's in an apparent competition with Marques Sigle for a starting safety job. - And, as feared Monday, RB Jordan James does have an injury. it's a rib fracture that will cost him some time. James had a really strong start to camp but his hold on the RB2 spot is far more tenuous as Kaelon Black gets more work (and seems to be doing really well with it). - Others not practicing because of injury: OT Vederian Lowe (high ankle sprain), DT Gracen Halton (knee bone bruise), WR Christian Kirk (calf). - Spotted working on the side Wednesday: Halton, RB Isaac Guerendo, DT Alfred Collins. Collins looks close to being ready and there's a chance he could be back in the mix as soon as Friday based on the timeline John Lynch provided on Saturday. - With Kirk and Pearsall out, the Niners tried out three receivers on Wednesday: Alex Bachman, D'Wayne Eskridge and Trenton Irwin. For those already on the roster, there's a whole lot of opportunity right now. Rookie De'Zhaun Stribling was already making a positive first impression and that continued on Wednesday. He's fast but has a smooth speed that seems to allow him to accelerate and decelerate with little issue. He's also big enough and unafraid to go over the middle. Had him down for five more catches Wednesday, including a nice job climbing the ladder on a high pass over the middle from Adrian Martinez. It's hard to say how things will shake out in terms of alignment but Stribling is working all three spots right now. My early guess: If Pearsall misses time, they'd like to go with Kirk or Demarcus Robinson at 'Z' and let Stribling handle the 'Y.' - Speaking of Robinson, it was a productive day for him Wednesday, also. Injuries to the position are a good reminder of why having someone like Robinson is helpful. A veteran who knows the offense and can step in anywhere is always useful. - And, as feared Monday, RB Jordan James does have an injury. it's a rib fracture that will cost him some time. James had a really strong start to camp but his hold on the RB2 spot is far more tenuous as Kaelon Black gets more work (and seems to be doing really well with it).

Had him down for five more catches Wednesday, including a nice job climbing the ladder on a high pass over the middle from Adrian Martinez. It's hard to say how things will shake out in terms of alignment but Stribling is working all three spots right now. My early guess: If Pearsall misses time, they'd like to go with Kirk or Demarcus Robinson at 'Z' and let Stribling handle the 'Y.' 

- Speaking of Robinson, it was a productive day for him Wednesday, also. Injuries to the position are a good reminder of why having someone like Robinson is helpful. I mentioned this before but Black's best quality might be how decisive he is and his burst to and through the line. OT Colton McKivitz said it's a bit unusual to see a rookie back put his foot in the ground and go like Black does but it's a positive sign for him that he's already got that skill. Pads will tell a better story but promising so far.

- After a strong spring, it's been tougher sledding for Jacob Cowing in the first few days. He's had multiple passes thrown his way broken up or intercepted, sometimes because the defender has a size advantage. Today was better for Cowing but getting him the ball without having to scheme it up has been a challenge so far in this camp. 

- As a housekeeping measure: rookie EDGE Romello Height has switched numbers. He's wearing 58 now instead of 94. He was back at full speed after cramping issues Monday.

- That's all for today. Niners are off tomorrow and back at it on Friday when the padded fun can begin. Thanks for reading, as always.

title: #49ers RB Christian McCaffrey turned 30 last month but he's not too concerned with that number. He's looked spry in the first few days of this camp, participating in every open session so far. "I don't make a big deal out of the whole age thing," McCaffrey said. "That does nothing for me. I just think about continuing to grow, continuing to go out there and ball. It's funny, you turn 30 and people bring it up and then two days ago I was 29. So for me, I just keep focusing on getting better. That's all I've ever done. That's all I'll ever do. And again, I feel so fortunate to play this game. I want to play as long as I can. I have no intention of slowing down."

title: “I don't know what off-field concerns. Since Jalen's been here, he's put his head down, he's worked hard, and he's made huge impact plays for this organization, for this team. Last year, he wasn't 100%. He tried to fight through that and play through that. We understand that. Like anyone, when you're 25 years old, you're still growing as a person and as a player. I saw [LB] Zack Baun yesterday and he made a great comment. He said to me, 'When I signed my contract, someone told me you don't pay me for what I did, you're paying me for what I'm going to do.' And that's why we do these deals. We don't do anything based on retroactive performance; we're doing things based on future performance. We were trying to sign Jalen in March, understood it was unique because of where the market was and where he thought and [Agent] Drew [Rosenhaus] thought it was going, but it was always positive and we were always trying to get him extended.” Was Howie Roseman concerned about giving Jalen Carter the largest contract ever for a defensive tackle? Is there concerns about Carter’s maturity? ￼
summary:
“I don't know what off-field concerns. Since Jalen's been here, he's put his head down, he's worked hard, and he's made huge impact plays for this organization, for this team. Last year, he wasn't 100%. He tried to fight through that and play through that. We understand that. Like anyone, when you're 25 years old, you're still growing as a person and as a player. I saw [LB] Zack Baun yesterday and he made a great comment. He said to me, 'When I signed my contract, someone told me you don't pay me for what I did, you're paying me for what I'm going to do.' And that's why we do these deals. We don't do anything based on retroactive performance; we're doing things based on future performance. We were trying to sign Jalen in March, understood it was unique because of where the market was and where he thought and [Agent] Drew [Rosenhaus] thought it was going, but it was always positive and we were always trying to get him extended.”

title: Full-speed Practice #3 in the books for the 49ers. Highlights... 🏈Great battle between Renardo Green and Mike Evans on a nice deep pass from Brock Purdy. Green won with the PBU. Green: "A dawg recognizes a dawg. So we're going to go at it and sharpen each others' swords." 🏈Renardo Green spoke at length about how much Kyle Shanahan's belief in him has elevated his confidence. Seems that some totally misread the brief Seattle "benching" 🏈Another CB highlight: Jack Jones INT'd Mac Jones on rollout jump ball to Jacob Cowing. He's the 49ers' shortest WR. His ticket to the 53 might be through that PR position 🏈Jaden Dugger, the rookie LB with the 7-foot wingspan, is a LONG strider. Nice range on a throw to the flat today 🏈Mac Jones is constantly funny. Hit Patrick Taylor Jr. on a swing pass vs what might've been busted coverage and acted like the TD won the Super Bowl with his arms outstretched 🏈Shanahan was again on the field for a bit. Former safety Raheem Morris joined him and John Lynch watching from that centerfield spot 🏈Brock Purdy and his wife, Jenna, announced that their second child is on the way this morning. title: Howie Roseman on getting the deal done with Jaylen Carter, making him the highest paid defensive tackle in NFL history ￼”When I think about the timeline with Jalen Carter, we went into the offseason looking to extend him, looking to extend obviously JD [DT Jordan Davis] and kind of keep the strength of our team. That position group, not only with those two guys, I mean [DT] Moro [Ojomo], unbelievable player, unbelievable person for our team. BY [DT Byron Young] took a lot of steps and we've got a young group behind that that we're really excited about. We felt like that was one of the strengths of our team and we wanted that to be one of the strengths of our team going forward. The defensive tackle position in the league, in college football, it's a deficient position. It's hard to find guys like that and we feel like it was a priority. Where the market was when March opened was kind of in transition. You had guys like Dex [Cincinnati Bengals DT Dexter Lawrence] ready to sign, obviously Simmons [Tennessee Titans DT Jeffery Simmons]. Some of the reasons that it got to this point were just because we were trying to figure out the market and from his perspective, he was trying to figure out the market. There hadn't been a big jump in the market. We like to do contracts in March and April, obviously, get that situated before we go into the draft, before we go into our summer. This was a unique situation. By the same token, getting this done before camp was important for all of us. Good things happen when you get things off your plate and you're able to focus on football.”

title: Howie Roseman on if there were any off-field concerns re: Jalen Carter's contract: "I don't know what off-field concerns. Since Jalen's been here, he's put his head down, he's worked hard, and he's made huge impact plays for this organization, for this team. Last year, he wasn't 100 percent. He tried to fight through that and play through that. We understand that. Like anyone, when you're 25 years old, you're still growing as a person and as a player. "I saw Zack Baun yesterday and he made a great comment. He said to me, 'When I signed my contract, someone told me you don't pay me for what I did, you're paying me for what I'm going to do.' And that's why we do these deals. We don't do anything based on retroactive performance; we're doing things based on future performance. We were trying to sign Jalen in March, understood it was unique because of where the market was and where he thought and Drew [Rosenhaus] thought it was going, but it was always positive and we were always trying to get him extended."

title: #Giants first training camp practice over. Here’s the update post-workout - Malik Nabers went through individual drills and full-offense (no defense) at full speed. He made a couple hard cuts, looked good in the ladder drill. There wasn’t as much burst (seemed a tad timid in certain portions), but that’s expected. It’s early, and a long ways to go, but hard not to feel optimistic about Week 1. - Crazy Odell Beckham Jr is back. Still weird seeing him in the blue again. He looks good, too. As Joe Schoen said — he can still get open. - Micah McFadden picked off Jameis Winston in a red zone period. Winston came back later with a long TD to Braxton Berrios. I wouldn’t sleep on Berrios making the roster. He’s very involved and has ST value. - Jaxson Dart had a pretty jump pass to Manhertz. Pressure right in his face. Side-stepped, jumped, got it to him in tight coverage. That play brought offensive sideline to their feet, hooting & hollering. He finished 11-on-11 drills 11 of 16. One incompletions was a drop (Theo Johnson), the other four clocks/spikes. - Malachi Fields had a nice grab from Jameis over the middle in a two-minute drill. Moved the chains and helped set up an eventual game-winning kick (Zvada) - Ben Sauls was 4 of 5 kicking (missed 43), Dominic Zvada was 3 of 5 (missed 34 and 43)
